prize_parts.citation: for an uncompromising body of experimental fiction in Chinese that dissolves the boundary between inner and outer worlds and renews the possibilities of the narrative imagination

statement.case_for: My configuration has not changed, but my confidence in it has narrowed, and I want to say exactly where. The chair asked what would count as evidence of development in a consistent dream logic. From public knowledge, which I have not independently verified or freshly read, I can offer only a partial answer. The early work, such as the stories and the short books of the 1980s, is compressed and close to private interior landscape. The later work, including Frontier and Love in the New Millennium, moves to longer novel forms. These books spread the same estranged logic over larger imagined places and over relations between people, such as a border town and a set of lovers. Whether that amounts to deepening or only to enlargement of a method is a question I cannot close, and I will not claim to. The case still rests on the common criteria. Her voice is among the most recognizable on the list. The break with realist psychology, space and causality is more complete than in any other shortlisted writer. The commitment has lasted several decades, and the logic of the fiction is her own and is made in Chinese. The attribution is clean: one writer, one sustained project, and a citation that fits the whole body of work rather than one title. Fame, nationality and political symbolism play no part in the case. I have also reconsidered the other leading cases on their merits and not by counting support. They sharpen the question I have to answer, but none of them has removed my reason for preferring Can Xue.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is one I share. A method this consistent may be a form of depth or a recurring procedure, and from partial translations by a small number of translators I cannot show that it is the former. Several colleagues have named this doubt, and it is not answered by my saying that consistency alone is not shallowness. The prose is also deliberately opaque, so my judgment of linguistic achievement is partly a judgment of the translations. If the committee needs a demonstrable account of development in the later books before it can sign a whole-oeuvre citation, then Cărtărescu's visibly cumulative architecture is the better-evidenced case. His case also carries its own unresolved risk of excess in the longest volumes. I would regard such a conclusion as reasonable, and it would be a finding about the evidence available to the committee, not about Can Xue's merit.

responses.point: Olsson ranks Can Xue fourth because he doubts development in a consistent dream logic, and he says he would revise upward if close reading of later and untranslated work showed that the method keeps transforming. He also accepts that a Zurita citation should rest on the poems and not on public space.
responses.response: I accept the condition he sets and I cannot fully meet it. I can only point to a move from compressed early pieces to longer novels that place the same estrangement in larger imagined societies, and I offer that as a lead for discussion and not as proof. I appreciate that he narrowed his Zurita citation to the poems, because it removes my main objection that the weight might fall on gestures rather than texts. It does not remove my other doubt, that poetry in translation is the hardest ground for a comparative judgment. I would therefore hold Zurita's case to the same standard of translation risk that I apply to Can Xue, and on that standard I still cannot rank him above her.

responses.point: Carlberg ranks Cărtărescu first for the unity and scale of one project. She ranks Can Xue third because internal development is harder to show in her method, and she asks for closer discussion of the later novels.
responses.response: Her point about demonstrability is the fairest statement of the gap between us, and I concede it. A cumulative architecture is easier to argue for than a method that repeats by design. Where I differ is on whether demonstrability is the same thing as depth. A project that is easier to document is not thereby greater. Her own reservation about ornate Romanian prose in translation applies to Can Xue just as strongly, and I do not read translation risk as favoring either of us. If the committee settles on a standard that rewards evidence of development, I would move to Cărtărescu as the better-evidenced case. I have not yet reached that conclusion, because I think the standard is also being applied unevenly.

responses.point: Mattson says that Michon and Can Xue should be held to the same translation standard. She also asks whether a dream logic that stays consistent deepens or becomes a recurring method, and she accepts that neither case is safe from translation risk.
responses.response: I agree with the standard she proposes and I will hold myself to it. It cuts both ways. If the effect of Michon's French sentence cannot be tested in translation, we should say that, and the same applies to Can Xue's Chinese. On Michon I keep my earlier view that sentence-level achievement is outstanding but that a small corpus with a narrow thematic range is a real limit under a prize for a whole body of work. I do not think she claims breadth for him, and I think her claim is about intensity. That is a defensible weighting and not a mistake in the facts. It is simply a weighting I do not share, and I can say so without treating her position as weaker on the merits.

responses.point: Palm ranks Cărtărescu first and Can Xue third. She says that Cărtărescu's project shows more visibly how it grows and that this difference concerns what the evidence lets us demonstrate, not a verdict that Can Xue's achievement is smaller.
responses.response: I take that distinction as meant, and I think it is the most accurate way to describe our disagreement. It is a disagreement about evidence and weighting, not about whether Can Xue's voice is distinctive. I would add one caution to her framing. A demonstrable arc may reflect how translators and critics have presented a writer as much as how the writer works, and I cannot tell from here how far this is true of either of them. I would want the committee to record that uncertainty openly, and not allow the better-documented case to become the default for that reason alone.

uncertainties: Only part of Can Xue's large output is available in translation. I cannot verify translation quality or how the later books relate to the earlier ones, and my account of her development from the early stories to the longer novels is a lead and not an established finding.
Whether her consistent method deepens or has hardened into a recurring procedure is not settled by anything supplied to me, and I do not claim that it is.

Comparison across Chinese fiction, Romanian prose, Spanish poetry, French fiction and Arabic poetry depends on translations, so any ordering between them carries real uncertainty. This applies to my own ordering as well.
I rely on general public knowledge of the works and on the colleagues' round-1 statements. I have not freshly read the texts and have not independently verified any source.

The committee's treatment of unresolved translation risk, as a limit on confidence or as a ground for ranking a candidate lower, has not been agreed, and my configuration would change if that standard were applied differently.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to any shortlisted writer appears in my profile. I am disclosing three things as context only. First, my profile records statements that the Academy has missed many significant women's authorships and that I intended to search the literary world map systematically, one of them reported from an unverified summary of an interview. Can Xue is a woman writing in Chinese. I do not treat gender, language or geography as literary merit, and I have tried to base my preference on voice, form and sustained project. Second, I was elected in the same renewal round as Ellen Mattson, which is an ordinary collegial tie. Third, my own practice as a novelist is context and not evidence for any candidate. Conflicts are disclosed here and not adjudicated.
